 7.2
  APPROVAL OF A SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH VASQUEZ & COMPANY LLP FOR ACCOUNTING AND
  INDEPENDENT AUDITING SERVICES

  Executive Summary:

  Staff recommends that City Council approve a second amendment to the professional
  services agreement with Vasquez & Company LLP authorizing the City Manager to
  increase total compensation by up to $10,000 annually. The request responds to
  increased audit demands and additional auditor hours resulting from staff turnover. The
  additional authority would apply to each of the four remaining fiscal years of the
  agreement, for a maximum potential increase of $40,000. (FIN)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends City Council adopt a resolution (Attachment 1) approving a second
  amendment to the Professional Services Agreement between the City of Lynwood and
  Vasquez & Company LLP (Attachment 2), authorizing the City Manager to increase the
  total compensation amount by up to $10,000 for each remaining fiscal year of the
  agreement, contingent upon prior approval by the City Manager for any additional work.
  The resulting not-to-exceed amounts would be $103,400 for the FY 2024–25 audit,
  $106,400 for the FY 2025–26 audit, $109,400 for the FY 2026–27 audit, and $112,500 for
  the FY 2027–28 audit.

 7.3 APPOINTMENT OF AN ALTERNATE BOARD MEMBER TO THE GATEWAY WATER
  MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY
  Executive Summary:

  The City currently has a vacancy in its GWMA Alternate Board Member seat, created
  when Pamela Torres was reassigned to other responsibilities. Staff recommends that the
  City Council adopt a resolution designating Javier Mendez, Water Operations Supervisor,
  as Alternate Board Member. In accordance with the GWMA Amended and Restated Joint
  Powers Agreement and the GWMA Bylaws, non-Legislative Body appointments to the
  GWMA Board must be made by resolution. There is no fiscal impact associated with the
  recommended action. (PW)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends City Council adopt a resolution (Attachment 1) appointing Javier
  Mendez, Water Operations Supervisor, as Alternate Board Member to the Governing
  Board of the Gateway Water Management Authority (GWMA), to serve continuously at the
  pleasure of the City or until the City Council designates a successor.

  7.4
  ACCEPTANCE OF $358,000 IN ADDITIONAL STATE GRANT FUNDING FOR
  ALAMEDA TRIANGLE ENVIRONMENTAL CLEANUP AND AMENDMENT OF THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2026–27 BUDGET

  Executive Summary:

  The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) awarded the City an
  additional $358,000 through Amendment 2 to the Office of Brownfields Equitable
  Community Revitalization Grant (ECRG) Round 2 award. The amendment increases the
  City’s total Round 2 award from $6,252,725 to $6,610,725. The funding would support
  eligible environmental cleanup, grant management, and related activities at the Alameda
  Triangle Site on Fernwood Avenue between Alameda Street and Imperial Highway.

  Site remediation must occur before the planned mixed-use development can proceed.
  Accepting the amended and restated agreement would allow the City to continue
  implementing the approved Remedial Action Plan and advancing the proposed
  commercial and affordable housing development. The additional grant does not require a
  local match. (CD)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends City Council:

  1. Accept Amendment 2 to the Equitable Community Revitalization Grant Round 2
  award from the California Department of Toxic Substances Control in the amount of
  $358,000;
  2. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute the Amended and Restated
  Agreement (Attachment 1) and any related documents, subject to approval as to
  form by the City Attorney’s Office; and
  3. Amend the Fiscal Year 2026–27 Adopted Budget and appropriate $358,000 to Fund
  3537.

 7.5 APPROPRIATION OF APPROXIMATELY $3.4 MILLION IN FEDERAL HOME AND
  HOME-ARP FUNDS FOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROGRAMS
  Executive Summary:

  Staff recommends that the City Council appropriate a total of $3,423,862.65 in existing
  federal housing funds for Fiscal Year 2026-27. The proposed appropriation consists of
  $1,800,000 in HOME Investment Partnerships Program (HOME) funds and
  $1,623,862.65 in HOME American Rescue Plan Program (HOME-ARP) funds.

  The HOME appropriation would provide budget authority for the reallocation that the City
  Council approved on August 18, 2026. The funds would support tenant-based rental
  assistance, property acquisition for affordable homeownership, and acquisition and

   rehabilitation costs.

  The HOME-ARP appropriation would fund eligible activities in the City’s approved
  Allocation Plan and Tenant-Based Rental Assistance Program Guidelines. These
  activities include professional and contractual services, housing assistance for qualifying
  populations, and project improvement costs.

  Approval would allow the City to use previously awarded federal funds for current and
  planned affordable housing activities and meet applicable United States Department of
  Housing and Urban Development (HUD) expenditure requirements. The recommended
  action would not affect the General Fund or require local matching funds. (CD)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends the City Council adopt a resolution (Attachment 1) appropriating
  $1,800,000 from the available HOME Investment Partnerships Program fund balance and
  $1,623,862.65 from the HOME American Rescue Plan Program carryover balance for
  Fiscal Year 2026–27.

 8.  NEW/OLD BUSINESS

 8.1 CITY COUNCIL CONSIDERATION OF POTENTIAL NAMES FOR THE RENAMING OF
  CESAR CHAVEZ LANE
  Executive Summary:

  On March 24, 2026, the City Council directed staff to move forward with the steps
  necessary to rename Cesar Chavez Lane, including a community engagement process.
  As part of that effort, the City conducted three community workshops and released a
  bilingual survey, which received 104 responses. Of those respondents, 73, or 70.2
  percent, indicated support for renaming the street.

  The Cesar Chavez Renaming Ad Hoc Committee met on September 14, 2026, to review
  the survey results and community feedback. Based on that feedback, the Ad Hoc
  Committee identified three potential names for City Council consideration: Beechwood
  Avenue, Rancho San Antonio Lane, and Lynwood Park Way. Council may also identify
  additional names for consideration. (CM)

  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends City Council:

  1. Review and consider the following potential replacement names identified by the
  Cesar Chavez Renaming Ad Hoc Committee:
  Beechwood Avenue;
  Rancho San Antonio Lane; or
  Lynwood Park Way; and
  2. Provide direction regarding the name or names to advance for further consideration,

 SUBJECT:
  APPROVAL OF A SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH VASQUEZ & COMPANY LLP FOR
  ACCOUNTING AND INDEPENDENT AUDITING SERVICES

 Recommendation:

 Staff recommends City Council adopt a resolution (Attachment 1) approving a second
 amendment to the Professional Services Agreement between the City of Lynwood and
 Vasquez & Company LLP (Attachment 2), authorizing the City Manager to increase the total
 compensation amount by up to $10,000 for each remaining fiscal year of the agreement,
 contingent upon prior approval by the City Manager for any additional work. The resulting not-
 to-exceed amounts would be $103,400 for the FY 2024–25 audit, $106,400 for the FY 2025–
 26 audit, $109,400 for the FY 2026–27 audit, and $112,500 for the FY 2027–28 audit.

 Executive Summary:

 Staff recommends that City Council approve a second amendment to the professional
 services agreement with Vasquez & Company LLP authorizing the City Manager to increase
 total compensation by up to $10,000 annually. The request responds to increased audit
 demands and additional auditor hours resulting from staff turnover. The additional authority
 would apply to each of the four remaining fiscal years of the agreement, for a maximum
 potential increase of $40,000. (FIN)

 Background:

City Council City Council Regular Meeting
  27
  In June 2024, the City entered into an agreement with Vasquez & Company LLP to provide
 accounting and independent auditing services to the Finance and Administration Department.
 Since execution of the agreement, Vasquez & Company LLP has provided professional
 accounting and independent auditing services.

 In April 2025, the City entered into a first amendment to the agreement to provide additional
 professional accounting services and revise the remaining compensation for independent
 auditing services. The first amendment established a not-to-exceed amount of $391,700 for
 professional accounting services and updated the annual audit fees for the remaining years of
 the agreement. All other terms and conditions of the original agreement remained unchanged
 and in full force and effect.

 The City is required to obtain independent audit services to ensure that its financial statements
 are audited in accordance with applicable federal and state requirements and generally
 accepted auditing standards. Under Government Code Section 12410.6(a), audits of local
 agencies must be performed by a certified public accountant or public accountant licensed by,
 and in good standing with, the California Board of Accountancy. Section 12410.6(b) further
 provides that a local agency may not employ a public accounting firm if the lead or
 coordinating audit partner having primary responsibility for the audit, or the audit partner
 responsible for reviewing the audit, has performed audit services for that agency for six
 consecutive fiscal years.

 Independent audit services provide an objective examination of the City's financial statements,
 internal controls, and financial activities; assist in evaluating compliance with applicable
 accounting principles, governmental auditing standards, and regulatory requirements; and
 support the preparation and issuance of the City's annual financial reports and related
 compliance filings and obligations.

City Council City Council Regular Meeting

  The proposed Second Amendment would authorize the City Manager to increase the
 remaining total compensation under the existing Professional Services Agreement by up to
 $10,000 annually. Use of the additional funds would be contingent upon prior approval by the
 City Manager. The additional compensation is intended to address extenuating circumstances
 that may require additional auditor hours to successfully complete the City's annual audit,
 while remaining within the original scope of services contemplated under the agreement. No
 changes are proposed to the scope of services, terms and conditions, or contract term. The
 agreement is set to expire no later than June 30, 2027. The agreement also includes two 1-
 year options to extend.

 The proposed amendment does not modify the overall scope of services provided under the
 original agreement. Rather, it would authorize the City Manager to increase remaining total
 compensation by up to $40,000, or up to $10,000 annually, to allow Vasquez & Company LLP
 to complete and continue to provide legally required auditing services for the remaining term
 of the agreement.

 Fiscal Impact:

 The proposed amendment would authorize the City Manager to increase annual
 compensation by up to $10,000, to be used only in extenuating circumstances requiring
 additional auditor hours to complete the audit. The maximum potential impact is $40,000 over
 the four remaining fiscal years of the agreement. Sufficient funding is budgeted within the FY
 2026–27 Adopted Finance and Administration Department General Fund Budget to cover the
 current-year amount, and staff would include any amounts for subsequent years in future
 proposed budgets. No additional appropriation is requested at this time.

  The Los Angeles Gateway Region Integrated Regional Water Management Joint Powers
 Authority, known as the Gateway Water Management Authority (GWMA), was formed in 2007
 in response to the passage of two voter-approved water bonds: Proposition 50, passed in
 2002, and Proposition 84, passed in 2006. The GWMA was formed to jointly prepare and
 adopt a regional plan for the management of water resources, and to implement and operate
 qualified projects and programs and prepare qualified reports and studies.

 Member entities of the GWMA include the cities of Artesia, Bell, Bell Gardens, Bellflower,
 Cerritos, Commerce, Cudahy, Downey, Hawaiian Gardens, Huntington Park, La Mirada,
 Lakewood, Long Beach, Lynwood, Maywood, Montebello, Norwalk, Paramount, Pico Rivera,
 Santa Fe Springs, Signal Hill, South Gate, Vernon, and Whittier, as well as the Central Basin
 Municipal Water District and the Long Beach Water Department.

 The Joint Powers Agreement establishing the GWMA calls for each member public agency to
 appoint, by name, a Board Member and Alternate Board Member to the GWMA Governing
 Board, which is the governing body of the Authority. Under the GWMA Bylaws, adopted on
 October 12, 2015, all non-Legislative Body appointments to the GWMA Board must be made
 by resolution; legislative body appointments may be made by minute order.

 On February 21, 2023, the City Council replaced the City’s previous GWMA appointees and
 designated the Director of Public Works as Board Member and Pamela Torres, Senior
 Management Analyst, as Alternate Board Member.

 Works, as Board Member, filling the vacancy created by the departure of the former Public
 Works Director. Ms. Torres has since been reassigned away from the responsibilities
 associated with the Alternate Board Member role, leaving the City without an active Alternate
 Board Member.

 Executive Summary:

 additional $358,000 through Amendment 2 to the Office of Brownfields Equitable Community
 Revitalization Grant (ECRG) Round 2 award. The amendment increases the City’s total Round
 2 award from $6,252,725 to $6,610,725. The funding would support eligible environmental

 Avenue between Alameda Street and Imperial Highway.

 Background:

 The Community Development Department has pursued outside funding to address
 contaminated properties that have constrained housing and economic development. The City,
 with assistance from Tierra West Advisors, Ramboll Americas, and Cox, Castle & Nicholson,
 submitted ECRG application ECRG-2023-01766 to support remediation of the Alameda
 Triangle Site. The City has studied and characterized the Site's environmental conditions for
 more than 16 years, but the high cost of remediation has been a barrier to redevelopment.

 DTSC previously awarded the City $426,217 through ECRG Round 1. That funding supported
 environmental review of the Site and preparation of a Remedial Action Plan (RAP). The
 completed plan allowed the City to apply for Round 2 implementation funding.

 On May 7, 2024, the City Council accepted the original ECRG Round 2 award and agreement
 in the amount of $6,252,725. Earlier this year, the City applied for additional funding to
 complete and close out the remediation of the site. In April 2026, DTSC approved Amendment
 2 for up to $358,000 in additional funding to reimburse eligible environmental activities and
 related costs.

 facilities and identified community input as an important consideration should the Council

 Cesar Chavez Lane extends from Birch Avenue to Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard adjacent

 Following Council direction, the City initiated a community engagement process to gather
 feedback regarding the potential renaming and possible replacement names.

 Community Engagement Process

 The City released a community survey on June 15, 2026, in both English and Spanish. The
 survey remained open through July 17, 2026, and was available to residents, business
 owners, and others with a connection to the City of Lynwood. The survey was completely
 anonymous.

 The survey was promoted through the City’s social media platforms using QR codes that
 linked directly to the English- and Spanish-language surveys. The survey was also
 incorporated into the City’s community workshops, where participants were encouraged to
 complete the survey and share comments as part of the discussion.

 In addition to the survey, the City held three community workshops:

  Tuesday, June 23, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m.
  Saturday, June 27, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m.
  Wednesday, July 1, 2026, from 5:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

 The workshops were intended to explain the community engagement process, provide
 historical context, gather community feedback, and outline the next steps in the process.

  Community Priorities and Considerations

 The survey also asked respondents what factors and qualities should guide the selection of a
 new street name.

 When asked what the City should consider, the most frequently selected responses were
 community identity, selected by 36 of 99 respondents, and historical significance, selected by
 22 of 99 respondents. When asked what qualities should guide a new name, the leading
 responses were honoring a local Lynwood figure or history, selected by 30 of 100
 respondents; reflecting Latino or Latinx heritage and culture, selected by 20 respondents; and
 honoring a woman or an underrepresented community member, selected by 18 respondents.

 Respondents also raised practical considerations associated with a potential name change,
 including changes to addresses and identification records, signage, mail and business
 materials, as well as potential navigation and customer confusion during a transition.
 Comments also reflected a preference for a name that is locally connected, culturally
 meaningful, inclusive, simple, and easy to remember, along with an interest in maintaining a
 transparent community role in the final selection process.

 Ad Hoc Committee Review

 The Cesar Chavez Renaming Ad Hoc Committee met on September 14, 2026, to review the
